candidates.statement: Need to find a new place when moving to a new neighborhood or a new country, usually by searching on the Internet with housing web apps.
context: moving to a new neighborhood or a new country

evidence_candidates.quote: Mainly when I move to a new neighborhood or to a new country, I need to find a new place. So I usually search on the Internet and use this type of web apps.

candidates.statement: Choose the neighborhood or place where to look for a house before searching by keywords.

evidence_candidates.quote: So usually I choose a neighborhood or a place where I want to find a house in, and then I start searching by such keywords

candidates.statement: Search by location keywords to find the websites relevant to that specific area and become familiar with which websites are most popular or most used there, especially in another country.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I want to be familiar with which websites are the most popular or most used there.
to find relevant websites for that specific area, because sometimes it's another country

candidates.statement: Check housing websites to see in which neighborhoods the options that fit my budget and requirements are clustered, as one way of choosing the area.

evidence_candidates.quote: One of the ways is when I check these types of websites that show houses and apartments available.

candidates.statement: Ask people who live in that country whether they recommend any places, as another way of choosing the area.

evidence_candidates.quote: the other other ways, is asking people who lives, for example in that country, if they have any recommendation for the places

candidates.statement: Pick a neighborhood close to where I usually go, such as a specific job or college, and search with that name.
context: when there is a specific job or college

evidence_candidates.quote: if I have a specific job, or if I'm studying at specific college, I will usually pick a neighborhood that's close to that area, and I'll start searching with that name.

candidates.statement: Search by the size of the place or bedroom counts, together with a budget limit.

evidence_candidates.quote: So actually, I will search by like the size of the place, or sometimes by bedroom counts. and with also a budget limit.

candidates.statement: Filter the many options down using non-important criteria such as amenities, extra features and how good looking the place is.

evidence_candidates.quote: after that, when I get many options, I can start filtering it down, using other non very important criteria

candidates.statement: After filtering, start contacting the providers; how fast they reply, whether they give enough information and their attitude affect my choices and help narrow the options down.
context: after filtering the options down to several

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes like how fast they will reply might affect my choices
which will help me also to narrow down my options

candidates.statement: When there is no reply, research the place by its name or find its location on Google Maps to get a website, URL or phone number and communicate by email or phone.
context: when the provider does not respond through the platform

evidence_candidates.quote: So I'll try to communicate with them using other methods like email or phone.
if it's an apartment that has specific name or finding their location in Google maps

candidates.statement: Total non-response from a provider is a bad sign that the management is not good.

evidence_candidates.quote: It's just a bad sign that the management is not very good, otherwise they won't just skip any type of communication.

candidates.statement: People put the information on these apps but do not stay active using the website; they rely on other channels.

evidence_candidates.quote: It seems like people put the information and not keep active using the website.

candidates.statement: Use the platforms mainly as a way to discover places while proceeding with communication outside these apps.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I mainly use this type of platforms like as a way to discover places. But I actually usually proceed with different type of communication outside of these apps.

candidates.statement: The app gives no visibility on the process: no last-update time, information may be outdated or wrong, the send-message form does not show how it is submitted, the provider feels unreachable, and there is no way to communicate in a short way.

evidence_candidates.quote: You don't know when was the time the information was lastly updated.
and if you click on, send a message, you will have this long form that you don't know how it will be submitted
You don't feel like you can communicate like in a short way.

candidates.statement: Seeing the last-update time and a small visual timeline of the next steps (and of what to expect if it fails) gives more trust and enthusiasm to engage.

evidence_candidates.quote: if I can see, like the information was last updated, for example, a week ago or 2 months ago
and I can see, like a small visual of the timeline that, like the website, can show me what are the next steps. If I fail, therefore, what should I expect?

candidates.statement: The form requires many fields that are not always known or wanted at that stage; I do not want to write a custom message or share much personal information, it feels overwhelming and makes me skip requesting through the website.
context: the form requires first name, last name, email, mobile number, move end date, beds, baths and a custom message

evidence_candidates.quote: And sometimes you don't want to share much information like email, phone, 1st name, last name, and all of them are required fields
It feels like overwhelming. So it makes me just get the information from the website and skip the process of requesting it through the website.

candidates.statement: Want an e-commerce-like flow: pick the listed option and see the expected response time, what happens next and deterministic steps.

evidence_candidates.quote: I would love like to know if I just proceeded with this option, what will happen when they would they respond to me? What will be next?

candidates.statement: Share personal information only after both parties confirm availability and interest; before that it is unnecessary and uncomfortable.

evidence_candidates.quote: I think like giving the information could be after confirming the availability from the 2 parties

candidates.statement: Current process: visit the site, log in, search with filters, view details; when interested, either fill the in-site form with unknown response time, or take the location from the map and find a phone or email elsewhere.

evidence_candidates.quote: when I get interested in one of the options. I will have 2 ways either to fill the form inside the website, and I never know when they will respond to me and how efficient is this process. or just to take their location from the map, then try to find more about them, using other websites like Google Map, where I might find a phone number or an email where I can communicate directly.

candidates.statement: Have a map with a drawing tool to circle the area to search in, because searching by neighborhood name is too specific.

evidence_candidates.quote: they provide sometimes a map with a drawing tool where you can just draw a circle around the place you're interested in in the map, and they will select the search inside that area

candidates.statement: Reviews from people make places feel more trusted and keep the information together.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, another thing that I like is providing reviews, I think reviews from people, makes. makes places feel more trusted, and could help let you have all the information together.

candidates.statement: Dislike extra steps such as being required to register and multiple unknown buttons; this long unknown process makes me skip the site and prefer sites with minimal options and a list of things to do.

evidence_candidates.quote: one of the things that I don't like is actually these extra steps like requiring you to register in the website.
So this type of long, unknown process makes me just skip the website and look for a website with like minimal options and and list things to do.

candidates.statement: Clicking favorites should save the item and it should be findable; currently I cannot find where it saves.

evidence_candidates.quote: there is a button called favorites. It should like, I assume as a normal user that if I click on favorites it should save the thing I'm looking for. But actually, I can't find where where it's saving it.

candidates.statement: The 'Request a tour' button leads to the same form as when interested, which feels weird.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also there is a button called Request a tour, and also it will have this form that you should fill, which is exactly when you were interested in the property.

candidates.statement: Being required to register just to do research throws me off the website.

evidence_candidates.quote: And also another thing is that when they require you to register just to do a research, so these things throws me off of the of the website.

candidates.statement: Want a comparison option to collect 3 or 4 options on a single page and look at the main features at the same time.

evidence_candidates.quote: I wish, if there is an option for comparison, like, sometimes I like 3 or 4 options like, I want to collect them all in in like a single page. So I can look in the main features at the same time.

candidates.statement: Favorites may be saving somewhere but I could not find it anywhere.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also the the favorites button is. It's really weird because it might be saving it somewhere. But actually, I couldn't find it anywhere.

candidates.statement: Favorites should be on the nav bar, or at least at the first level of the menu.

evidence_candidates.quote: It should be like on the nav bar, or at least at the menu, at the like 1st level of the menu.

candidates.statement: Registration or login should not be required; it could be optional for saving information and pre-filling it.
candidates.modality: should not be required / could be optional

evidence_candidates.quote: It could be optional thing like if you want your information saved and to be filled directly you can register. But it should not be required.

candidates.statement: The user can communicate with the provider without an account; there is no need for such personalization.

evidence_candidates.quote: since I think the user can just communicate with the with the house provider without the need of being registered or having a specific account

candidates.statement: Just start searching and see the whole functionality directly.

evidence_candidates.quote: Just start searching and seeing the whole functionality directly.

candidates.statement: Be more convenient: search the information I want without steps I do not believe are beneficial.

evidence_candidates.quote: It's like to be more convenient just to search the information you want without having steps that you don't believe it's beneficial.

candidates.statement: Search by location and then filter by price range, number of beds and baths, home type, and extra criteria such as move-in date, pets and utilities.

evidence_candidates.quote: You can filter by price range. you can filter by the number of beds and baths you can also filter by the home type whether you want a house, an apartment. and also you can filter by extra criteria, like the move-in date, or any other things that you want, like allowing pets, for example, having utilities, and so on.

candidates.statement: Like that the filters are optional and do not force entering everything, because I am sometimes not sure what I want.

evidence_candidates.quote: I like that. The filters are optional. They don't enforce you to enter everything, because sometimes you're not very assured about what do you want

candidates.statement: Fear losing options whose owners did not specify a criterion; want an option to also allow the unspecified ones and see both kinds.

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe I would love if there is an option where I can have like. I can also allow the people who didn't specify, so I can see both

candidates.statement: Filtering by a criterion shows only the options that confirmed it, losing the ones where the owner did not specify.

evidence_candidates.quote: So when I just filtered by allowing a pet, they will just show for me the ones that has confirmed.

candidates.statement: Add a checkbox called 'include' to also show options that did not determine the criterion.

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe if there is like a check box called include, for example, like the options that didn't determine, or something like that.

candidates.statement: With the checkbox I get both the ones that allowed and the ones that did not specify; without it only the ones that specify they allow.

evidence_candidates.quote: The one who allowed and the one who didn't specify, and if I didn't click on the checkbox, I will have the ones who only specify that they allow.

candidates.statement: Search and filters plus the sites collecting many options give an overview of price ranges, available options, reviews and locations, information I might not get otherwise.
context: especially when moving to another country

evidence_candidates.quote: So I want to be able to know what are the options? And what are the price ranges, and so on.
these types of filters, and also these types of websites will collect a lot of options together will give me an overview about the price ranges

candidates.statement: Website rules enforcing a standard photo format for owners would give people more trust.

evidence_candidates.quote: So maybe if the website has some sort of rules that enforces people who own these properties to take the picture in a specific format

candidates.statement: Really want to see when the listing information was last updated, because it might not be accurate or up to date.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, another thing that I would really love is to have to be able to see when it was last updated.

candidates.statement: People put little effort into photos, or make them look better than reality, which can change a person's mind about a good place.

evidence_candidates.quote: People don't put much effort in the pictures which could lead the person to change his mind, although the place is is good, and sometimes people try to make the pictures look better than the reality.

candidates.statement: No information on the details page seems unimportant; it seems good as it is.

evidence_candidates.quote: I can't see, like any information that it's not really important, like It seems good to me

candidates.statement: The details feel sufficient; only the last-updated information is missing.

evidence_candidates.quote: Oh, it feels sufficient. It's only the part where I said about like when it was last updated.

candidates.statement: The details shown (address, pictures, price diagram, units available, features, reviews) are sufficient; I just want to be assured that it is up to date.

evidence_candidates.quote: I think, like there is sufficient information. It just. I just want to be assured that it's it's up to date.

candidates.statement: Mention again the wish for a feature that helps compare between several options.

evidence_candidates.quote: I wish, if there is such feature that helps me to compare

candidates.statement: Would be very good to have all communication with property owners through these websites on a single platform, if the process were clear and fast.

evidence_candidates.quote: You just have a vague button called. Send a message where you will fill a form and never know what will happen next.

candidates.statement: Changing the UI to give insight into how the communication process works would make the user trust the feature and keep the communication on the website.

evidence_candidates.quote: So maybe it's changing something in in the ui to make the user have some insight about, how would the communication process be?
This will make him like, trust the feature more, and never try something else, and just keep the communication in in the website.

candidates.statement: Providers may reply very fast, but the UX does not make me trust it; it is not clear to me.

evidence_candidates.quote: They might reply like, very, very fast, but it's not clear to me.
